finding: Encrypted editing now uses an owner-authenticated plaintext working copy and fails closed otherwise.
evidence: All mutation-capable pdf-lib loaders now reject encrypted bytes. The store decrypts through PDFium only after owner authentication; a user-password-only open remains read-only until the owner password is supplied. encrypted-edit.test.ts proves encrypted bytes are rejected and an owner-decrypt, rotate, re-encrypt result reopens with both user and owner passwords while preserving content.
impact: The prior corruption path is closed; unsupported encrypted editing cannot silently produce unreadable output.
fix: Retain the encrypted edit-save-reopen fixture and add AES-128 and legacy RC4 interoperability fixtures when licensed samples are available.

finding: Redaction now recursively removes and verifies images inside nested Form XObjects.
evidence: walkPageObjects recursively traverses Form XObjects, accumulates their matrices, fails on unreadable objects/bounds/matrices, and removes children through FPDFFormObj_RemoveObject. The post-save verifier uses the same traversal. Tests prove nested-image removal and forced failure when PDFium refuses the removal; Poppler renders the result with the image replaced by the redaction box.
impact: The confirmed nested-image bypass no longer reports false success.
fix: Retain the nested and transformed Form-XObject corpus and extend independent verification to annotations, attachments, metadata, and optional-content policy.

finding: Page deletion rebuilds from surviving pages instead of retaining detached page objects.
evidence: deletePages now creates a fresh document through extractPages using only survivor indexes. The regression scan confirms the deleted page's unique text is absent from every decoded indirect stream while surviving text remains. Poppler reopens and renders the survivor page correctly.
impact: Deleted-page content is no longer retained through the confirmed unreferenced-object path.
fix: Keep the forensic stream scan mandatory and add safe outline, named-destination, and page-label remapping to reduce the rebuild tradeoff.

finding: Unconfirmed browser downloads no longer clear the unsaved state.
evidence: The anchor-download branch now reports PDF copy downloaded and returns before markSaved, persistence, or editing-session cleanup. An in-browser test created and edited a blank PDF, clicked Save without a file handle, observed the download-copy notice, and confirmed both Unsaved edits indicators and Discard remained visible.
impact: Blocked or cancelled browser downloads can no longer remove the user's unsaved-edit warning.
fix: Retain the browser regression and add automated coverage for picker cancellation, write failure, and edits arriving during an awaited write.

finding: The public download and repository paths are still dead.
evidence: On 2026-07-12, /download, /download/windows, github.com/naumanahmed19/pdfeditor, and its releases path returned 404. The homepage crawl again found both public GitHub links broken.
impact: The acquisition funnel ends before installation, verification, or purchase.
fix: Publish one supported release URL with signed installers, checksums, release notes, and a working upgrade path, then replace every CTA.

finding: Available installer artifacts are untrusted, stale, and inconsistently versioned.
evidence: The Jul 8 artifacts are older than main da01514. Authenticode reports unsigned artifacts or UnknownError for CN=PickPDF Test Code Signing. PickPDF 0.1.1 is unsigned while package.json, Tauri, Cargo, and About remain 0.1.0.
impact: No available installer contains the audited fixes, Windows trust warnings remain, and users cannot identify the current release.
fix: Create a reproducible release pipeline with one version source, a production signing identity, trusted timestamping, artifact verification, SBOM, checksums, and rollback-capable updates.

finding: The desktop and both live origins still lack baseline browser security controls.
evidence: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:27-33 still sets csp:null. Automated checks scored pickpdf.app and open.pickpdf.app 25/100 because HSTS, CSP, frame protection, MIME protection, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy were absent.
impact: Injection, clickjacking, downgrade, and data-exposure incidents are harder to contain.
fix: Ship a restrictive tested CSP and all six baseline response headers on both origins and in the desktop WebView.
source: source audit and live header checks

finding: Public commercial and enterprise claims still exceed delivered capability.
evidence: Compression and crop wording improved, but public/download and live pricing still present large-file performance, always-offline behavior, updates/support, file associations, central seats, silent deployment, PO billing, priority support, checkout, and DPA delivery as available while the product and legal pages show these systems are absent or planned.
impact: The claims create refund, procurement, privacy, and reputational risk.
fix: Remove every unverified claim, mark Pro and Team as preview until delivery exists, and link each material promise to a tested capability or policy.
source: source, live copy, and product audit

finding: Three guide pages in the sitemap still canonicalize to the guides hub.
evidence: The three detail URLs return 200 but declare https://pickpdf.app/guides as canonical. The sitemap still contains 23 URLs and lists every lastmod as 2026-07-09.
impact: Search engines are told to consolidate the guide pages instead of indexing them.
fix: Give each complete guide a self-referencing canonical, or remove unfinished guide URLs from the sitemap.

finding: Page structure preservation improved but remains incomplete.
evidence: Delete and move now preserve surviving catalog structures and extract/merge re-register copied forms. However, src/lib/pdftools.ts:203-218 and 427-451 omit outlines, named destinations, and page labels for extract/merge; deleted destinations can dangle; duplicate/insert paths do not re-register imported fields.
impact: Some page workflows can still damage navigation, form behavior, labels, and document semantics.
fix: Preserve and remap every catalog structure per operation, define signature invalidation behavior, and validate round trips in Acrobat, Foxit, PDFium, and qpdf.

finding: Word and text conversion silently replaces unsupported Unicode characters with question marks.
evidence: src/lib/createpdf.ts:45 and 453 sanitize every text run to WinAnsi before drawing with standard Helvetica fonts. The test suite confirms unsupported characters are replaced with ?. The Create PDF screen warns about tables, images, columns, and fonts, but does not disclose script or character loss.
impact: Arabic, CJK, Indic, emoji, and other non-WinAnsi text can be corrupted while the conversion still reports success.
fix: Embed fonts with broad Unicode coverage, shape complex scripts, preserve font fallback per run, fail or warn before lossy conversion, and add multilingual DOCX/TXT fixtures.

finding: Permission enforcement remains bypassable through several workflows.
evidence: Shared permission decoding and multiple store gates were added, but split/extract, text/HTML/DOCX/image export, OCR, and search/replace are not centrally gated. The assemble-document permission bit is not modeled.
impact: Restricted documents can be copied, assembled, or modified through alternate paths.
fix: Enforce permissions inside every mutation and export service, then test each operation under every permission combination.

finding: Undo history is capped by step count rather than memory and can retain discarded PDF proxies.
evidence: src/store.tsx:861-911 retains up to 60 full byte snapshots. Redo-tail and cap trimming do not destroy every dropped proxy; close paths do not consistently destroy distinct historical proxies.
impact: Large files and long sessions can exhaust memory or crash the editor.
fix: Use a byte budget, deltas or temporary files, and deterministic disposal for every discarded PDFium handle.

finding: Rendering remains synchronous, non-cancellable, and unbounded.
evidence: src/lib/engine.ts:449-458 returns a no-op cancellation function; page rendering allocates a PDFium bitmap plus a full RGBA copy without pixel limits; viewer startup loads page handles for the document.
impact: Large or malicious PDFs can freeze the UI or exhaust memory.
fix: Move rendering and extraction to workers, tile pages, add real cancellation, and enforce page, pixel, file, and time budgets.

finding: Unsafe link schemes, arbitrary AI endpoints, and plaintext API-key storage remain.
evidence: PDF links are placed into anchors without a strict scheme allow-list; user link schemes are preserved and opened without confirmation; custom AI endpoints accept arbitrary URLs; customApiKey is serialized to localStorage.
impact: A malicious document or injection can launch unsafe protocols or expose provider credentials.
fix: Allow-list safe schemes, require HTTPS except loopback, confirm external launches, and store desktop secrets in the OS credential vault.

finding: Local retention is disclosed better but remains hard to control.
evidence: The 80 MB autosave cutoff is now visible, but IndexedDB still keeps up to ten documents and closing only marks them closed. There is no no-retention mode, document delete-all control, or surfaced quota/private-mode failure. Chat still retains 40 messages.
impact: Regulated users cannot define or prove local data-retention behavior.
fix: Add ephemeral mode, per-document and clear-all deletion, a storage dashboard, retention settings, and visible persistence failures.

finding: The editor remains inaccessible for important keyboard and screen-reader workflows.
evidence: About and Confirm improved, but Password, Print, Properties, Security, Sign, and Signature modals lack complete dialog semantics and focus management. PDF form overlays lack programmatic labels, object editing is pointer-only, placed text uses an unnamed contenteditable, and small targets remain.
impact: Users with assistive technology are blocked and enterprise or public-sector procurement will fail.
fix: Adopt one accessible modal primitive, label every control, add keyboard object editing, enforce target sizes, and add axe plus keyboard end-to-end tests.

finding: Unit coverage grew sharply, but release-critical system coverage is still absent.
evidence: The stop-ship fix working tree passes 297 tests in 28 files, up from 79 tests in the first audit. The repository still has no CI, coverage, accessibility, broad corpus, interoperability, fuzz, or meaningful Rust test suite. test-fixtures is untracked and unused.
impact: Critical save, encryption, redaction, distribution, and accessibility failures can still reach a release.
fix: Create a tracked golden corpus and CI gates that open, edit, save, reopen, render, extract, validate, and compare output across multiple PDF engines.

finding: Certificate signing is useful but not yet a trusted professional signature stack.
evidence: HEAD adds RSA .p12/.pfx CMS signing and local cryptographic verification with eight tests. It lacks OS trust-store validation, ECDSA, revocation, RFC 3161 timestamps, LTV, smartcards, incremental saves, and a warning before signature-breaking edits.
impact: Users can create a cryptographic signature but cannot establish full signer trust, long-term validity, or safe multi-signature workflows.
fix: Add incremental signing, chain/revocation validation, timestamps and LTV, ECDSA, OS certificate stores, and explicit invalidation UX before building recipient workflows.

finding: The production editor payload and default local AI model remain heavy.
evidence: The main build emits a 2.266 MB main JS chunk, a 404.85 KB document-conversion chunk, 4.634 MB PDFium WASM, 23.567 MB ONNX runtime WASM, and a 541 KB worker. Static imports defeat several intended dynamic chunks; the default local model is about 3 GB and asks for about 8 GB RAM.
impact: Cold start and first-use completion suffer on low-end devices and slower networks.
fix: Split engines by workflow, lazy-load PDFium and AI runtimes, choose a smaller default model, and publish p75 first-page and interaction benchmarks.

finding: The browser editor origin still serves indexable soft-200 shells.
evidence: open.pickpdf.app /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, and a random nonexistent path all returned the same 730-byte HTML shell with HTTP 200. The shell has no noindex, canonical, description, or X-Robots-Tag.
impact: The origin creates duplicate-brand, crawl-noise, and soft-404 risk.
fix: Return real 404s for unknown paths and send X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow on the application shell.

finding: Thirteen sitemap routes still have no inbound HTML links.
evidence: All eight tool pages, all four comparison pages, and /guides are reachable from the sitemap but not from crawlable HTML navigation.
impact: Crawl priority, authority flow, usability, and commercial conversion remain weak.
fix: Create linked tools, comparison, and guide hubs; make homepage feature tiles real links; and cross-link related jobs.

finding: Commercial, guide, and legal pages remain too thin to compete or establish trust.
evidence: Current visible counts including shared chrome are roughly 101-129 words for tools, 65-78 for comparisons, 73-81 for guide articles, 91 for Teams, and 102-112 for legal pages. The automated crawler also flagged six reachable pages below 300 words.
impact: The pages do not satisfy task intent, show expertise, or support privacy and procurement claims.
fix: Add task-specific workflows, screenshots, limitations, examples, authorship, evidence, related links, and complete legal terms.

finding: Search metadata and the homepage H1 remain systematically weak.
evidence: Twenty-two of 23 descriptions are under 120 characters, the homepage description is 180, six titles are under 30, and pricing is 67. The homepage H1 remains 'Where productivity meets privacy' instead of identifying a PDF editor.
impact: Query relevance and organic click-through potential remain weaker than necessary.
fix: Write unique intent-matched titles, descriptions, and H1s for every indexable route.

finding: The site still lacks the identity and evidence layer needed for a privacy product.
evidence: /about, /contact, /security, /trust, /changelog, /.well-known/security.txt, /authors, and /case-studies return 404. Only the homepage has JSON-LD; no Organization, WebSite, Article, or BreadcrumbList graph is present.
impact: Users, search engines, and enterprise buyers cannot validate the operator, security posture, authorship, or product claims.
fix: Publish company identity, named team and authors, contact and security channels, changelog, privacy architecture, benchmark methodology, case studies, and structured data.

finding: Workflow, collaboration, platform, and enterprise systems remain absent.
evidence: Main da01514 does not add shared review, version history, e-sign routing, batch workflow automation, CLI/API/SDK/webhooks, cloud or DMS connectors, macOS/mobile distribution, SSO/SCIM/RBAC, audit logs, policy controls, or admin analytics.
impact: PickPDF cannot replace category leaders for teams, regulated buyers, or cross-platform users.
fix: Win the private local-first solo workflow first, then add optional collaboration, automation, integrations, platforms, and enterprise controls in measured stages.

finding: Main is synchronized, but no immutable release snapshot identifies the shipped product.
evidence: Local main and origin/main both resolve to da01514 after a fast-forward pull. Existing installers predate this commit, and no release tag or manifest identifies a shipped source snapshot.
impact: The branch drift is resolved, but installer, website, and source can still refer to different products without traceable release identity.
fix: Use protected main, signed release tags, generated version metadata, a release manifest, and one audited commit per artifact set.

finding: The deployed marketing application is still absent from the tracked checkout.
evidence: The live site exposes 23 routes, but the repository contains only the standalone public/download page. The untracked marketing folder contains launch-video assets, not the deployed router, sitemap, legal, or page source.
impact: SEO, claims, legal copy, redirects, and security headers cannot be reviewed or gated with the product release.
fix: Version the marketing application and infrastructure, add preview deployments, and run crawl, claims, link, schema, and header checks in CI.

finding: Release and third-party compliance artifacts are missing.
evidence: The repository has no LICENSE, NOTICE or third-party inventory, SECURITY policy, CHANGELOG, EULA, or tracked legal documents. Cargo metadata still says 'A Tauri App', authors ['you'], with blank license and repository fields.
impact: A paid installer cannot demonstrate redistribution rights, vulnerability reporting, support terms, or release provenance.
fix: Complete product metadata, choose a license, inventory redistributed dependencies and fonts, publish notices and security policy, and track release/legal documents.

finding: Main includes useful professional features with documented fidelity limits.
evidence: Paragraph growth can overlap content below; annotation import reconstructs a reduced internal model and can lose rich native properties; layer toggles ignore locked/app-state semantics; PDF/A is heuristic preflight rather than certification; OCR processes the whole document in one selected language; Create PDF is lossy for unsupported Unicode.
impact: The broader feature set increases regression surface and can create round-trip loss if marketed as full professional parity.
fix: Expose limitations in UI, add preservation fixtures, and gate each feature on cross-viewer output invariants before release.

finding: The site has pageview analytics but no verified product conversion instrumentation.
evidence: Plausible loads on the marketing site, but the production bundle contains no explicit download, browser-open, Pro, or Team-lead events. The Team lead path uses mailto rather than durable server-side capture.
impact: The team cannot measure or improve the acquisition-to-activation funnel.
fix: Track privacy-safe CTA and activation events while keeping document contents and editor behavior out of marketing analytics.

finding: AI-search readiness remains minimal.
evidence: /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt return 404; AI crawlers inherit the wildcard robots rule; only the homepage has JSON-LD.
impact: Answer engines have little structured evidence to identify and cite the product.
fix: Add a concise llms.txt, explicit crawler policy, entity and article schema, named authors, and citable benchmark data.

finding: Production Core Web Vitals remain unverified.
evidence: The PageSpeed API returned rate-limit responses and no field data. No Search Console, CrUX, RUM, or real-device traces were available.
impact: No reliable p75 LCP, INP, or CLS claim can be made.
fix: Connect Search Console and CrUX, add privacy-safe RUM on marketing pages, and test representative mobile devices.

finding: The synchronized main snapshot passes all available local gates.
evidence: The stop-ship fix working tree based on main da01514 passes typecheck, production build, 297/297 tests across 28 files, npm audit with zero advisories, and cargo test with zero Rust tests.
impact: The codebase has a stronger unit-test baseline than in the first audit.
fix: Keep these gates and add the missing release-level suites.

finding: Three prior correctness or trust blockers are fixed.
evidence: Revision-based dirty tracking now covers byte edits; one shared coordinate system covers 0/90/180/270 degrees and offset CropBoxes; crop and compression copy now describes their limits honestly. These areas have dedicated regression tests.
impact: Close warnings, rotated placement, and crop/compression expectations are materially safer.
fix: Retain the regression tests and include them in mandatory CI.
